objection.status: error reported by an ordinary grader
objection.quote: If every two members of $\mathcal F$ intersect, then there are finitely many nonempty finite sets $B_1,\ldots,B_s\subseteq P$ such that...
objection.witness: The lemma is false. Let F_k={x_0,…,x_k,y_k} for distinct symbols. These sets pairwise intersect at x_0, but T_n={y_0,…,y_{n-1},x_n} are infinitely many distinct inclusion-minimal finite transversals, impossible for an up-set generated by finitely many B_j.
